overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the inaccurate-minutes complaint, because the complainant could not identify any inaccurate portion, and declined to review the remaining complaints and the Public Media Center allegation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's October 19, 2016 meeting minutes were inaccurate.
allegations.key_passage: As the complainant was unable to identify any portion of the minutes that he believed to be inaccurate, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the recordings of the October 19, 2016 and January 18, 2017 meetings were edited.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, we decline to review the remaining four complaints filed with the Board.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notes used to create the October 19, 2016 minutes were destroyed.
allegations.key_passage: Any complaints involving public records requests and/or municipal records retention may be resolved by contacting the Supervisor of Records within the Secretary of the Commonwealth's Office.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to provide documentation substantiating the chair's statements at the January 18, 2017 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, we decline to review the remaining four complaints filed with the Board.

allegations.summary: One complaint alleged the Woburn Public Media Center, a 501(c)(3) corporation, violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Generally, 501(c)(3) corporations are not public bodies subject to the Open Meeting Law.
